judged_text: The data migration interpolates the admin-configured embeddable_hosts setting value directly into a raw SQL INSERT: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)", so any single quote or backslash in a stored host string is executed as SQL. An attacker (or a merely careless admin) who set SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts to a value containing a quote before this migration runs — e.g. "x'); DROP TABLE embeddable_hosts;--" or "a','b'); UPDATE site_settings ..." — gets arbitrary SQL executed against the production database at deploy time; the migration is the config-backed sink and no escaping or parameterization is applied to #{h}.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the prior SiteSetting 'embeddable_hosts' value from the DB, splits it, and then performs `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` for each entry. `h` is interpolated directly into raw SQL without quoting/escaping or parameterization, so a value containing a single quote can break the SQL and could be leveraged for SQL injection during migration execution (at minimum, it can cause deploy-time migration failure/data corruption).
